title: Neurosurgeon Salary in Australia: Hourly Rates, Annual Pay, and Tax for 2026-27
description: Learn how to calculate a neurosurgeon salary from hourly rates, typical hours, and tax. Includes Fair Work award rates, super, and fortnightly pay estimates.
salarySummary: Based on typical full-time hours of 57 per week, a neurosurgeon's annual salary can exceed $400,000 before tax, but actual earnings depend on experience, location, and practice type.

faqs.q: How is a neurosurgeon salary calculated from an hourly rate?
faqs.a: Multiply the hourly rate by the number of hours worked per week, then by 52 weeks. For example, if a neurosurgeon earns $200 per hour and works 57 hours per week (the average for this occupation according to the Australian Bureau of Statistics), the annual gross salary is $200 × 57 × 52 = $592,800. The [the timesheet](/) on this site lets you enter your own hourly rate and hours to see the annual, fortnightly, and weekly equivalents, including tax and super estimates.

faqs.q: What is the typical hourly rate for a neurosurgeon in Australia?
faqs.a: Neurosurgeon hourly rates vary widely. The Medical Practitioners Award [MA000031] sets minimum rates for employed doctors, but most neurosurgeons are above award. The Australian Bureau of Statistics reports median full-time adult ordinary time earnings of $2,083.70 per week across all occupations, but neurosurgeons earn significantly more. A common range for employed neurosurgeons is $150–$300 per hour, while private practice earnings can be higher. Use the [pay guides](/blog) from the Fair Work Ombudsman to check minimum award rates for your classification.

faqs.q: Does the neurosurgeon salary include superannuation?
faqs.a: No, the salary figure typically quoted is before super. Under the Superannuation Guarantee, employers must pay an additional 12% of ordinary earnings into your super fund, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year (2026-27). For example, on a $400,000 salary, super is calculated on the first $270,830, giving $32,499.60 in super. The [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page explains how salary packaging can affect your take-home pay.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Neurosurgeon Salary in Australia

When you search for a **neurosurgeon salary**, you'll find figures that range from $300,000 to over $600,000 annually. But how do you convert an hourly rate into a meaningful annual figure? This article explains the calculation, the typical hours neurosurgeons work, and how tax and super affect your take-home pay.

### The Basic Formula: Hourly × Hours × 52

The standard way to estimate annual gross pay is:

**Annual salary ≈ hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**

This formula assumes you work the same number of hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. For most employees, the benchmark is a 38-hour week, as used in the National Minimum Wage. However, neurosurgeons typically work much longer hours.

According to the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) 2021 Census data, neurosurgeons work an average of **57 hours per week** when employed full-time, and 86% work full-time hours. That's well above the all-occupations average of 44 hours. So when calculating a neurosurgeon salary, using 38 hours would significantly underestimate actual earnings.

### Example: Converting an Hourly Rate to Annual Pay

Let's say a neurosurgeon earns $250 per hour. Using the typical 57-hour week:

- Weekly: $250 × 57 = $14,250
- Fortnightly: $14,250 × 2 = $28,500
- Annual: $14,250 × 52 = $741,000

If you prefer to use the standard 38-hour week for comparison with other roles, the annual figure would be $250 × 38 × 52 = $494,000. The [the timesheet](/) on this site lets you toggle between hours and see the difference instantly.

### Award Rates and the National Minimum Wage

The Fair Work Ombudsman publishes pay guides for each award. Neurosurgeons are covered by the **Medical Practitioners Award [MA000031]**. This award sets minimum hourly rates for different classifications of medical practitioners. However, most neurosurgeons are employed above the award rate, or work in private practice where earnings are negotiated individually.

For context, the National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour for a 38-hour week, or $1,004.90 per week. Casual employees receive a 25% loading, making the casual minimum $33.05 per hour. Neurosurgeon salaries are far above these minimums, but the award provides a safety net for conditions like overtime, penalties, and leave.

### Tax on a Neurosurgeon Salary

Once you have your annual gross figure, you need to estimate tax. For the 2026-27 financial year, the resident tax rates are:

- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus a Medicare levy of 2% (with possible exemptions or surcharges).

Using the $741,000 example above, the tax would be substantial. The [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page can help you estimate after-tax income, but remember that HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not included in this basic calculator.

### Superannuation: Paid on Top

Employers must pay superannuation guarantee contributions of 12% of ordinary earnings, up to a maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year (2026-27). For a neurosurgeon earning $741,000, super is calculated only on the first $270,830, giving a maximum super contribution of $32,499.60 per year. This is paid on top of the salary, not deducted from it.

If you are a contractor or self-employed, you may need to arrange your own super. The [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page has more detail.

### Fortnightly Pay and Budgeting

Many employers pay fortnightly. Using the example above:

- Fortnightly gross: $28,500
- After tax and Medicare (estimated): approximately $16,000–$17,000, depending on deductions and offsets.

Knowing your fortnightly amount helps with budgeting and comparing job offers. The [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) page explains how to switch between pay periods.

### What the Data Says About Neurosurgeon Earnings

The ABS does not publish median weekly earnings specifically for neurosurgeons in its Survey of Employee Earnings and Hours, but the Jobs and Skills Australia profile shows that neurosurgeons are among the highest-paid medical specialists. The median age is 44, and only 18% are female. The long hours (57 per week average) reflect the demanding nature of the role.

### Limitations of This Calculation

This estimate assumes:
- The same hourly rate for every hour worked (no overtime or penalty rates)
- No unpaid leave
- No salary sacrifice or packaging
- Full tax-free threshold claimed
- No HELP or other study loan repayments

For a precise determination of your pay and tax, consult a qualified accountant or use the ATO's tax calculator. The [reference tables](/data) on this site provide historical award rates and tax tables for further comparison.

### Summary

A neurosurgeon salary is best estimated by using the actual hours worked (often 57 per week) rather than the standard 38. Use the formula hourly × hours × 52 to get annual gross, then apply tax and super. The Fair Work Ombudsman's pay guides and the ABS data are the most reliable sources for benchmarks. Whether you're negotiating a contract or planning your finances, understanding these components helps you make informed decisions.
